solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Golfer arranged to host a quiet game

indicators.note: to host means the shuffled letters hold the next pieces inside them
arranged means the letters of golfer are put into a new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A golfer has set up a children's game for a quiet moment on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns GOLFER into LEFROG, which hosts A and P (quiet) after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground game in which children vault over one another's bent backs.

clue.text: Sound equipment covered by large light

indicators.note: covered by in a down clue means the equipment sits below the letter for large

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an amp is an amplifier for sound

explanation.surface: Audio gear sits under a big light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives illumination, a light.

clue.text: Try a couple of times to accommodate part-time worker

indicators.note: to accommodate means the pair of letters hold the worker inside

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them give TT
a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: Someone tries more than once to find room for a part-timer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort to achieve something, a try.

clue.text: Way to support film events regularly lacking journalists

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means the road word sits beneath the other letters
regularly lacking means every other letter of film events is dropped, keeping the odd ones

parts.note: a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: Journalists are absent from film events, which follow a set route.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEET STREET in London was home to the national newspapers, so the name stands for the British press.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet Street is used by metonymy for British national journalism and the people who work in it.

clue.text: Lots of pasta, with no topping

indicators.note: with no topping in a down clue means the top, first, letter is removed

parts.note: noodles are a kind of pasta

explanation.surface: A big plate of pasta served without sauce on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, plenty.

clue.text: Consul regularly heading for overseas city

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Consul, the even ones here
heading for means the first letter of the word overseas

explanation.surface: A consul is posted to a foreign city, travelling there on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, so a straightforward example of a city.

clue.text: A doctor visiting South Australia and somewhere in the Pacific

indicators.note: visiting means the pieces go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Australian state
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor travels to South Australia and then on to a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Occasionally switch positions?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: intermittently, now and then
second meaning: the two settings of a light switch

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading is literal: the two positions of a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intermittently and also names the two states a power switch can be in.

clue.text: Ancient mound: yours truly covering over the top

indicators.note: covering means the setter's word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: yours truly is the setter referring to themself, giving ME

explanation.surface: The setter claims to have covered an old earthwork, perhaps excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: A motte is the earth mound of a Norman motte-and-bailey castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motte is a raised earthwork on which a medieval keep was built, an ancient artificial hill.

clue.text: Cover put over Jane Austen novel, or Catch-22?

indicators.note: put over in an across clue means turned over, so the word for cover is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Someone puts a dust jacket on a copy of Emma, or wonders about Heller's novel Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' looks like placing a dust jacket on the book, but it signals turning the cover word round; Catch-22 is also a novel, adding to the bookish disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catch-22 is a no-win situation, which is a dilemma: a choice between equally bad options.

clue.text: Adorable old barking dog

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of adorable old go crazy

explanation.surface: A sweet elderly dog yaps away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise, but as British slang for mad it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A labradoodle is a crossbreed of Labrador retriever and poodle, a type of dog.

clue.text: Second panel covering the right PC component

indicators.note: covering means the combined pieces wrap around the others

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a board is a panel

explanation.surface: A second panel is fitted over the right-hand side of a computer part.
explanation.definitionFit: The motherboard is the main circuit board of a personal computer, holding processor and memory.

clue.text: Individual taking a stand with regards to sibling

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a sister is a sibling

explanation.surface: A person makes a stand over something to do with a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A resister is someone who opposes or refuses to comply, taking a stand against something.

clue.text: Car in back of garage, say

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the word garage

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A car sits at the back of a garage, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain an estate is a car type with an extended rear load space, a station wagon.

clue.text: Disagreement about another void list of charges

indicators.note: about means the quarrel word goes around those two letters

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: void means another is emptied of its inside letters, leaving its outer pair

explanation.surface: Customers argue over yet another empty price list.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or fees, such as those for a hotel or utility.

clue.text: Knowledge, in a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Knowledge, in one sense of the word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sense' reads as a hedge; it is really IN plus one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is deep understanding of something, a form of knowledge.

clue.text: Plain fish, mostly dry on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside means the shortened word goes within the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of dry is dropped

explanation.surface: A plain fish that is mostly dry inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the fish but is a noun: a flat treeless region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast flat, treeless Arctic region, a plain.

clue.text: One nurse could possibly like sceptical people?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of nurse could may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse wonders whether she could resemble doubting people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptical people are disbelieving, which is exactly what incredulous describes.

clue.text: Some humorous sarcasm held up as insensitive

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
Some means only part of the words humorous sarcasm is used

explanation.surface: A bit of humorous sarcasm is pointed to as tactless.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly lacking sensitivity or refinement, blunt and tactless.

clue.text: Cry about everything

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone wails about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A call is a shout or cry, as of a bird or a person.

clue.text: Prepared bagels maybe do taste fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic suggests wild invention, so the letters of do taste are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Bagels prepared a certain way taste fantastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagels are often served toasted, so this describes how they may be readied for eating.

clue.text: Belief in Supreme Being rejected by many atheists initially

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: God is the Supreme Being
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, taken as many

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of atheists

explanation.surface: Many atheists reject belief in a Supreme Being.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held principle or tenet laid down as true, a belief.

clue.text: Device runs application

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
use is the application of something

explanation.surface: A gadget runs an app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Device' and 'application' paint a phone running software; the device is a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A device in the sense of a scheme or stratagem is a trick meant to deceive.

clue.text: Pay up front with a loan from Mum and Dad?

indicators.note: up front means the first letter of Pay

parts.note: a rental is a hiring out, loosely a loan

explanation.surface: Someone pays in advance using money lent by their parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental describes anything coming from one's parents, mother and father.
